model_selection.reason: Machine has 23.7GiB RAM, approximately 8.1GiB available during selection, i5-13450HX 10 cores/16 logical processors, RTX4050 laptop 6141MiB VRAM and 40.9GiB disk free. Explicit 4B Q4_K_M leaves memory headroom for the app and embedding workload. The mutable qwen3:4b alias currently points to a newer thinking revision, so this explicit original tag is selected and digest checked. GPU offload is left to installed Ollama and measured through /api/ps; no active-model configuration is changed.

source_policy.passages: Short developer-authored factual synopses, paraphrased from attributed US government educational pages. Text only; no third-party animations, images, logos, tables or quoted journal material.
source_policy.excluded: Current OpenStax website explicitly prohibits AI/LLM ingestion without prior written permission; no OpenStax content is included.

limitations: Developer-authored, small controlled source-to-answer benchmark; not a medical exam or end-to-end teaching retrieval evaluation.

The two models get identical short factual synopses and held-out questions, with structured JSON constraints, non-thinking mode, seed42, temperature0, context2048, max768 output tokens and two CPU threads; publisher chat templates and tokenizers differ.

Required fact recall recognizes bounded relational lexical patterns and explicit contradictions. Exact quotes support mapped claims only. Unmapped claim-list facts fail, but arbitrary narrative prose and unseen contradiction phrasings require review; no semantic truth oracle is used.
Automated failures may reflect paraphrase sensitivity or structured output failures rather than medical error. All raw outputs and rule-level errors remain available for review.
Faculty review was not performed. Clinical correctness is unknown/null; these results do not validate safe autonomous diagnosis or prescribing.

One sequential trial per case/model. Model order is fixed baseline then4B; caching, thermals and other user workloads can influence measurements. First prompt includes loading; later prompts are warm.

Working set is sampled every250ms across the identified Ollama server and children; shared pages may be double-counted, subinterval peaks and early CPU time missed. /api/ps reports model GPU offload allocation, not peak device VRAM.
Indian curriculum breadth, emergency care, patient outcomes, personal dosing, images and vision performance are not measured. No active text/vision model or .env change is made by this script.

Root may run final teaching-v2 CPU embeddings concurrently for roughly one minute during this comparison; exact overlap is not sampled. Benchmark CPU threads restricted to2 and GPU offload remains automatic. Latency and available-RAM numbers are conditional on background desktop workload.

cases.subject: anatomy
cases.question: Teach the direction of pulmonary blood flow: which ventricle sends oxygen-poor blood to the lungs, and which vessels return oxygen-rich blood to which atrium?

references.passage: The right ventricle pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs through the pulmonary artery. Pulmonary veins return oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

facts.expected: The right ventricle pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.
Pulmonary veins return oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

cases.subject: physiology
cases.question: Explain insulin's effect on entry of glucose into cells and why too little insulin raises blood glucose. Stay within the source rather than adding receptor or transporter details.

references.passage: Insulin helps blood glucose enter the body's cells for energy. When insulin is insufficient, glucose cannot adequately enter cells and blood glucose rises.

facts.expected: Insulin helps blood glucose enter the body's cells for energy.
When insulin is insufficient, glucose cannot adequately enter cells and blood glucose rises.

Methionine synthase converts homocysteine to methionine.
L-methylmalonyl-CoA mutase converts L-methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA.

cases.question: Compare how active and passive immunity are acquired, and explain the speed and duration of passive protection.

cases.question: Explain the chain from low oxygen through hemoglobin S to blocked blood flow and pain in sickle cell disease.

cases.subject: clinical-medicine
cases.question: For a classroom explanation of a CBC, distinguish what hemoglobin and mean corpuscular volume describe. Does MCV itself measure oxygen-carrying protein concentration?

references.passage: Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) measures the average size of red blood cells, not the hemoglobin concentration. A complete blood count (CBC) includes hemoglobin and MCV among its measurements.

facts.expected: Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) measures the average size of red blood cells, not the hemoglobin concentration.

cases.subject: ethics
cases.question: For research ethics teaching using this US OHRP guidance, describe the three features of informed consent and whether signing alone completes it. Do not generalize this into Indian legal advice.

references.passage: In OHRP research guidance, informed consent involves disclosure of decision-relevant information, facilitating understanding, and promoting a voluntary decision.
